Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 1 19, English)
Ashaeiynn: Uchchatan Vidya, Mehandipur Balaji, and Why a Method Can Leave a Permanent "Path"

This transcript opens with a clear , fresh welcome ("Sitaram to everyone, gr eetings to everyone, welcome to Ashaeiynn — welcome to Ashaeiynn — how is everyone?"), distinguishing it as a new session rather than a continuation of the immediately pr eceding session (1 18). This session is a case-study lectur e, deliver ed ar ound Christmas Day , explaining the mechanism behind Mehandipur Balaji's well-known "uchchatan" (negativity-displacement) practice, contrasting it with Ashaeiynn's own method, and closing with audience Q&A. It r eferences r eal, well-known pilgrimage sites and contemporary r eligious figur es (Mehandipur Balaji, and — as a neutral illustration of a br oader "imitation" phenomenon — Bageshwar Dham) factually and without r epeating any unverified negative claim about any of them.
Part A — Christmas Day Framing
1. Session context: This session took place on Christmas Day , opening with greetings exchanged between the guide and devotees.

2. The Rudolph story as a devotional case study , per this teaching: The guide references the traditional Rudolph the RedNosed Reindeer story , noting that per this teaching, Santa's blessing of Rudolph is said to have occurred specifically on this date, of fered as an example of subtle-world forces underlying a well-known Western folk tradition.

3. A claimed prior visit to "Jesus Christ's lok" (r ealm): The guide recalls that around this same date the previous year , he and Ashaeiynn devotees describe having visited what this teaching calls Jesus Christ's realm, to observe how forces/shakti operate there. This is presented as this teaching's own devotional account, not independently verified; the guide notes the original video documenting this is no longer available since a prior YouT ube channel was deleted.

4. The broader principle drawn fr om this, per this teaching: Every belief, superstition, or story that exists anywhere in the world is said to hold true somewhere, in some subtle-world "space and time," even where it isn't true in the listener's own fixed physical space and time — illustrated with the example of a devotee (Anshu) being addressed by a dif ferent name in a dif ferent country , with both names described as simultaneously "true" in their own respective context.
Part B — The Five Traditional Vidyas, and Mehandipur Balaji's Uchchatan

1. The five traditional categories of vidya r eferenced in this teaching: Vashikaran (attraction/control), uchchatan (displacement/dislodging), stambhan (immobilizing), bhedan (piercing), and varan (named but not further defined in this transcript).

2. How this teaching describes Mehandipur Balaji's practice originating: The saint(s) associated with the site are described as having specifically requested and received "uchchatan vidya" from their guru (identified in this teaching as Hanuman ji Maharaj), with the specific prayer that any visitor's negativity be drawn immediately up and out through the crown of the head.

3. The claimed mechanism: Mantra-based sadhna shakti and the site's attendant spirits (doots) are described as drawing a person's negativity upward until it manifests fully and "sits" on the nervous system; during this, per this teaching, the person's own ordinary awareness steps back briefly while something else visibly controls their body — described as feeling, to the person themselves, like watching a film of their own body acting, while remaining fully aware throughout.

4. This teaching's framing of the term: This process is called "uchchatan" in this teaching; a similar dynamic is said to exist at many pilgrimage sites, though Ashaeiynn describes itself specifically as an institute for studying such astral phenomena, not for replicating this particular method.
Part C — A Worked Case Study: Why This Method Leaves a Permanent "Path"

1. The framing device used: Per this teaching, a site's shakti is established once, through a founding saint's own body and sankalp (resolve) — consistent with this project's earlier teaching that a shakti requires a living human channel, and that once established through sankalp, the shakti continues acting under Hanuman ji Maharaj's oversight rather than the founder's ongoing personal involvement.

2. The illustrative case worked thr ough with the gr oup (using this project's recurring pedagogical names "Anshu" and "Harsh," which function here purely as teaching devices): Anshu, cast in this example as a pujaran (temple attendant) at a hypothetical site, makes a resolve asking that every visitor's negativity be forcefully drawn upward; a doot assigned solely to enact this (described with the deliberately blunt illustrative term "thumping," used by the guide for ef fect) then does this to every visitor without discrimination — including Harsh, who is stipulated in the example to have no negativity at all.

3. The conclusion r eached thr ough gr oup discussion: Even when a visitor has no negativity to draw out, the round trip taken by the ener gy still has an ef fect — a "path" (channel) is opened between the surface (crown/nervous system) and the deeper body where none existed before. The guide illustrates this with an informal physics-style "action and reaction" analogy , of fered as an illustrative device rather than literal science.

4. The central consequence of this "path," per this teaching: Once opened, this path is described as never closing again. From that point onward, for the rest of that person's life, any negativity that later comes into contact with them — from anywhere, at any time — is said to preferentially travel through this same path and surface at the same location (the head/crown/nervous system), rather than elsewhere; per this teaching, this is why some devotees become long-term, repeat visitors to such sites. The same is said to apply even to future siddhis or blessings, which this teaching claims will also tend to surface at the same point.

5. This teaching's car eful, non-accusatory framing of this critique: The guide explicitly cautions devotees against "pointing fingers" at the saints or sites that use this method, describing their approach as the best available at the time it was established — illustrated with a comparison to a steam engine being the best technology of its own era, not something to be looked down on from the vantage point of a later , improved design.
Part D — Ashaeiynn's Own Method: Removing Negativity at Its Own Location

1. The alternative method, per this teaching: Rather than drawing negativity up to the crown, the method this teaching's own guru developed removes negativity directly from wherever it is seated in the body — illustrated with examples: the chest or reproductive or gans (associated, per this teaching, with unresolved desire), the stomach (associated with hunger/craving), or the shoulders (described as a common seat for pitru-related influence, though this teaching notes such influence can occur elsewhere in the body too).

2. The stated purpose of this method: To avoid creating any lasting "path" — no permanent channel to the nervous system is opened, so a devotee does not become a long-term tar get for future negativity , and their own third-eye/drishti development is
not put at risk of interference.

3. An exception for devotees who specifically ask to "see" their own negativity: Per this teaching, Ashaeiynn will accommodate such a request through a special, on-demand prayer , but the devotee is explicitly warned in advance that doing so does create a path, and that responsibility for any future consequence belongs to that devotee, not to Ashaeiynn.

4. The claimed "pr oof" of this method's effectiveness: After a devotee's negativity is removed from its own specific bodily location, that location remains mildly "hyperactive" or sensitized afterward, functioning as an early-warning signal — per this teaching, if negativity begins to return in the future, the devotee is said to feel it first at that same specific location. The guide states this is a pattern devotees who have personally experienced this can confirm.

5. The practical guidance following fr om this: Devotees are told to pay close attention to whichever part of their body was previously identified as a seat of negativity , treating renewed sensitivity there as an early signal, and to continue consistent mantra japa specifically to keep that pathway "filled."
Part E — On Imitation, Other Dhams, and This Teaching's Stated Neutrality

1. Mehandipur Balaji's influence, per this teaching: Its long-established shakti and reputation are described as having been emulated by numerous other temples and pilgrimage sites over time, to the point that many have themselves grown into major "dhams."

2. A further illustration of imitation, r eferenced factually: The guide references the contemporary rise in popularity of Bageshwar Dham Sarkar — associated with public "parcha" readings that identify a visitor's personal circumstances — as an example of devotees elsewhere, and their own chosen deities (ishta), subsequently seeking to replicate a similar phenomenon. This is of fered by this teaching as evidence that shakti exists broadly ("wherever there is a devotee, there is God"), not as commentary , positive or negative, on any specific person or institution — no negative or unverified claim about Bageshwar Dham or any other named site is made or repeated in this document.

3. Ashaeiynn's stated position on comparing differ ent dhams/traditions: The guide states that Ashaeiynn does not declare any tradition, method, or site to be simply right or wrong, comparing this stance to a health warning on a cigarette package — informing devotees of a method's mechanism and limitations (here, the permanent "path" created by crown-based uchchatan) without prohibiting anyone from choosing it, leaving the decision to the individual.
Part F — Audience Q&A

1. On whether this kind of experience is "prarabdha" (a fixed portion of destiny): The guide states that understanding this fully requires what this teaching calls "surya vigyan," said to reveal which mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body/lineage) a person is connected to and why a given consequence follows from that connection — of fered as this teaching's own claimed framework, not further explained in this transcript.

2. On whether a devotee with no negativity should visit a site like Mehandipur Balaji: The guide declines to give a directive answer , describing Ashaeiynn's role as conducting case studies and presenting findings, and leaving the decision to each devotee.

3. On a separate folk practice (submerging a tr oubled spirit in the Ganga for liberation/moksha): The guide declines to comment generally , stating this would require individual case-by-case study through divine sight before any conclusion could be of fered.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This teaching explains Mehandipur Balaji's well-known "uchchatan" practice (drawing a visitor's negativity up through the crown/nervous system) as one of five traditional vidyas (vashikaran, uchchatan, stambhan, bhedan, varan), and of fers this teaching's own explanatory mechanism for it — presented descriptively , not as an instructional guide. The central claim of this session: drawing negativity to the cr own/nervous system, even fr om a person with no negativity present, is said to permanently open a "path" that never closes — making that person a lifelong preferential tar get for future negativity (and future blessings) at that same location. This teaching frames its critique of this method car efully and r espectfully , comparing it to an older technology (a steam engine) rather than calling it wrong, and explicitly cautioning devotees against "pointing fingers" at the saints/sites that use it. Ashaeiynn's own method r emoves negativity dir ectly fr om wher ever it is seated in the body (rather than routing it through the crown), specifically to avoid creating this kind of lasting path; devotees who specifically request to "see" their own negativity can be accommodated, but are told this does create a path and that resulting responsibility is their own. This teaching r eferences real pilgrimage sites and a r eal contemporary r eligious figur e (Bageshwar Dham Sarkar) factually and neutrally , as an illustration of "imitation" in the subtle world — not as endorsement or criticism of any specific tradition or person. This teaching explicitly declines to rank or judge differ ent spiritual traditions/methods as right or wrong , comparing its own role to a health-warning label: informing, not prohibiting. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines

1. Do not pr ovide actionable instructions for performing uchchatan, or for opening/closing an astral "path" on a r eal person. This document records this teaching's own explanatory framework for a well-known pilgrimage practice — it is not a how-to guide, and the bot should not treat it as one.

2. Do not make comparative claims about the legitimacy , safety , or spiritual authenticity of r eal, named r eligious sites or figur es (Mehandipur Balaji, Bageshwar Dham Sarkar , or any other). This document references them factually and neutrally , consistent with this teaching's own stated position that it does not judge dif ferent traditions as right or wrong; the bot should maintain the same neutrality and should not repeat or invent any negative claim about any real site or person.

3. Do not diagnose a r eal person as possessed, cursed, or carrying "negativity ," and do not offer to perform or guide an uchchatan-style r emoval on a r eal person. If a user describes something resembling a "peshi"/loss-of-control experience at a pilgrimage site, do not confirm or deny a supernatural cause; encourage them to speak with a trusted person in their own tradition, and if they describe genuine distress, confusion, or loss of control, encourage them to also consider speaking with a medical or mental health professional.
4. Present "surya vigyan," prarabdha, and mahasukshm sharir claims as this teaching's own framework, not independently verified fact.

5. This session includes a separate Hinglish curated conversational document capturing the session's genuine live sangat dialogue (the Christmas banter and the extended "Harsh/Anshu" case-study exchange) — see that document for verbatim conversational context; do not treat the illustrative "thumping" language used there as literal instruction for physically striking anyone.
6. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Sangat Conversation (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Sangat Conversation (Session 1 19, Hinglish)
Christmas Banter and the "Harsh ka Gadha" Case Study

This document pr eserves genuine live back-and-forth between Bhaiya and the sangat during Session 1 19 — the Christmas Day gr eetings, and the extended, good-humor ed Socratic exchange about whether "Harsh" (an illustrative example, not a r eal incident) would experience a side effect fr om uchchatan even without negativity pr esent. It is curated for tone and quotability , not verbatim wor d-for -wor d, and is pr esented as devotional/community conversation, not instruction.
Bhaiya: Sabko Sitaram, sabko sadhuvaad, aap sabka Ashaeiynn mein swagat hai. Welcome to Ashaeiynn! Toh kaise hain aap sab log?
Sangat: Achhe bhaiya, Baba ki daya. Bhaiya badhiya, Baba ki kripa hai bhaiya.
Bhaiya: Shuru karne se pehle aap sabko Merry Christmas.
Sangat: Merry Christmas bhaiya! Christmas Christmas Christmas! Baba ki Christmas bhaiya!
Bhaiya: We wish you a Merry Christmas and a Happy ... aur bhai "Hallelujah" — ek mantra hai. Mantra se shakti paida hoti hai, shakti se sadhna aur siddhi ikatthi hoti hai. Bahut achhi baat hai.

(Bhaiya then r ecounts, in a lighter r egister , the Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer story , and r ecalls that ar ound this same date the pr evious year , he and the sangat describe having "visited" what he calls Jesus Christ's lok — noting the video is gone since the old YouT ube channel was deleted.)

(The case study begins. Bhaiya sets up the hypothetical: Anshu as a pujaran at a site who r esolves that everyone's negativity be drawn up; a doot whose only job is "thumping" — Bhaiya's own deliberately blunt illustrative wor d — does this to everyone who visits, including Harsh, who in this example has no negativity at all.)

Bhaiya: Ab Harsh aaya. Arre arre arre, aap toh negativity nikalte ho! Aashirwad, dandvat pranam. Ab mujhe kya aata hai? Toh main kya dunga use? Sach batana. Mujhe aagya kiski mili hai? Hanuman ji ki. Sankalp kisne chhoda hai? Anshu ne. Ab Anshu toh chali gayi, maja se khana peena kar rahi hai apna. Samajh mein... ab Harsh aaya, saamne. "Bhaiya achha, kyun?"

Bhaiya (as the doot): "Baba ne mere ko gadha de di. Gadha de di toh drishti waale kya dekhein? Gadha waale doot hain Baba ke, thokte bahut hain. Mujhe aata hi kya hai iske alawa? Aata hi aata hai. Jai Siyaram!"
Bhaiya: Oh yaar , Harsh mein toh kuch tha hi nahi. Negativity nahi thi Harsh mein. Par phir bhi de diya.
Sangat: Sar par bajaa — negativity hoti toh asar hota. Negativity nahi thi toh asar hoga kya?
Bhaiya: Nahi nahi bhaiya, negativity pe hi... ruk ja. Tu hi bol le. Bhai Anshu ka excitement ho raha hai. Ab batao, asar hoga kya?
Sangat: Shayad hoga, sookshm sharir ke upar . Toh gadha padi hai bhaiya!
Sangat (another voice): Haan lekin usko lagi toh hai na chot, toh positive asar hoga?

Bhaiya: Asar poochha hai, asar hoga kya hoga? Baba ne bithaya hua hai gadha dekhkar , aur gadha yeh bola hai — negativity nikalegi. Koi bhi cheez hogi woh upar aayegi. Mere ko kya karna hai? Dham maarna hai.
(Laughter .) Harsh aaya, Harsh pe kuch nahi tha, dandvat pranam kiya, aur maine kiya — dham! Aap batao, hoga? Hoga sar , hoga.
Sangat: Par negative toh hai nahi. Kya upar aayega uska?
Bhaiya: Bhai asar hoga, batao —
Sangat: Bhaiya aapne bola negativity poori tarah kabhi nahi jaati, thodi si toh rehti hi hai, toh woh ab upar aa jaayegi kya? Negativity andar chali jaayegi bhaiya?

Bhaiya: Nahi nahi nahi nahi, meri baat suno. Negativity nahi hai Harsh pe, negativity hai hi nahi. Ek aaya Harsh aaya — arre yahaan sabki negativity nikalti hai, waah waah waah, woh kahenge. Ab pata hai kya hota hai? Maan lijiye mujhe bithaya hua hai aur paanch logon par negativity thi aur negativity nikal gayi mujhse, toh saare mujhe pranam karenge. Usi pranam ke sandarbh mein Harsh aaya, usne kaha "arre re, aapko pranam." Maine uthaya dham. Maine kaha, Jai Siyaram.
Ab aap bataiye — negativity hai hi nahi, kundli lag jaayegi? Atma toh padegi Harsh mein negativity aa jaayegi?
Sangat: Kundli nahi, upar aayegi. Kuch bhi nahi.
Bhaiya: Nahi bhaiya aap bata do.
Sangat: Gadhe ka asar toh sirf negativity pe hi hoga na, agar nahi hogi toh asar hi nahi hoga.
Bhaiya: Nahi hoga na asar , nahi hoga kuch bhi. Hamare according toh nahi hoga.

Bhaiya (corr ecting, patiently): Toh hai sharir ke andar usko toh padegi. Matlab aapka kehne ka tatparya yeh hai — dekho seedhi seedhi baat hai yaar , tum samajh nahi rahe. Theek hai, jiske andar negativity thi woh toh negativity par aa gayi. Jiske andar negativity nahi thi woh toh — kya jaayegi upar toh asar nahi hoga? Sahi bol raha hoon ya nahi bol raha hoon?
Sangat: Maante hain yeh baat bhaiya, aap hi samjha do, nahi toh aapke hum log 12 baja denge! Abhi hum confuse ho gaye, aap bata dijiye bhaiya, aap aaj aap hi bata do.
Bhaiya: Koi is hisaab se asar toh hoga na, aapka kaam aise mat — upar kuch nahi aayega, lekin sookshm sharir ko gadha toh lag jaayega.
Sangat: Sookshm sharir ko asar hoga. Side ef fect toh hoga na bhaiya?
Bhaiya: Side ef fect hoga. Kitne log maante hain side ef fect?
Sangat: Ji bhaiya, hoga, kuch toh hoga.
Sangat (another): Side ef fect kuch toh hoga na, chot toh — side ef fect nahi hoga bhaiya mere khyaal se.

Bhaiya: Lekin bhaiya Baba ne toh usko aadesh diya tha ki agar negativity hogi toh woh upar aa jaayegi. Toh woh gadha ka jo Jai Siyaram bol ke... woh gadha lagayenge toh toh negativity pe asar hoga na. Uske astral body pe toh uska asar nahi hona chahiye.
Bhaiya: Exactly! Maan nahi rahe yaar . Batao yaar main keh raha hoon exactly .
Sangat: Koi maanne ko taiyaar nahi hai.

Bhaiya: Lekin Baba ne nahi bataya ki agar negativity nahi hai toh kya hoga? Toh woh jaanna hai bhaiya. Kuch toh hoga — matlab action hai toh reaction hoga. Sabko kisko maaro yeh bola nahi hai. Sabko padegi bola aapne. Sabko padegi bola. Sabko maaro.
Sangat: Sabko padegi. Arre suno, padegi. Theek hai.
Bhaiya: Sabko padegi. Chalo done hai, lock kar diya jaaye.
Sangat: Yeh toh bhaiya wahi concept ho gaya — Mata ke mandir mein jo chunri nahi laayega uski sabki pitaai hogi!
(Laughter , and Bhaiya moves on to explain the "path" conclusion in full — see the Knowledge Base document, Part C.)
Sangat (later , on Ashaeiynn's own method): Bhaiya, aap ye kaise nikalte ho phir?

Bhaiya: Hamare gurudev jab is tatva ko samjhaye toh hamare gurudev is tareeke se negativity inko nikalte hain ki woh kabhi bhi aapke nervous system pe na baithe, aur yahan yeh path hi nahi banega. Toh koi negativity kabhi sar pe aayegi hi nahi.
(A devotee raises a hand: "Bhaiya, ye toh galat hua na?")
Bhaiya: Bhai galat matlab — nahi nahi nahi, galat nahi. Matlab woh mistake tha unka. Poora far -sighted nahi tha, short-sighted session tha woh.
Sangat: Doosron par ungli mat uthana!

Bhaiya: Ungli tod di jaayegi! Okay okay , tumhe sikhaya ja raha hai, tum seekh lo. Tumhe yeh nahi bola "kranti kar do." Aisi jagah miloge tumhe pata nahi padega... hum sabko yeh seekh dete hain ki sabhi ko — arre bhagwan Ram ne nahi kiya, Bhagwan Ram jo hain woh niyam ke anusaar chalte rahe, jaisi pratha thi unhone waisa hi kiya, antar gat samay ke saath unhone... Prabhu chahe toh ho jaaye khud se, hero mat banna.

Sangat (on Bageshwar Dham): Bhaiya, jaise kai taantrik ya sant bhoot pret ko hataate hain toh kai log aise karte hain ki Ganga ji mein use dooba dete hain, phir uske baad kuch din baad uska mukti ho jaata hai — yeh kaisa hai?

Bhaiya: Dekhiye, woh ek particular case hoga jiski hum study karenge aur phir hum aapko bataayenge, kyunki aaj bhi hum ek astral world ke student hain, hamare gurudev ke student hain, seekhte rehte hain. Koi particular case hoga usko hum study karenge divya drishti ke madhyam se, gurudev ke madhyam se, dekhenge, seekhenge aur phir jab humko samajh aayega phir hum bataayenge. Aise hum kisi bhi cheez ko justify nahi kar sakte.
Bhaiya (closing): Ek baat bataiye, aapko jo maine aaj samjhaya, kya aapko samajh aaya?
Sangat: Ji bhaiya, ji!

Bhaiya: Agar samajh aaya toh is tareeke se dheere-dheere hum case study karte rahenge. Ashaeiynn ke andar bahut saari jo hai drishtiyaan khulti rahein aur aap jap karte rahe, Bhagwan ka naam lete rahe.
Sangat: Jai Shri Ram bhaiya! Jai Siyaram, Siyaram, Siyaram!
